sections.heading: Aristotle's On Virtues and Vices
paragraphs: This is the Greek text of περὶ Ἀρετῶν καὶ Κακιῶν (conventionally "On Virtues and Vices").

This work is pseudo-Aristotelian: it survives in the Aristotelian corpus (and was long read as his) but is judged by modern scholarship NOT to be by Aristotle himself - stated here plainly, as scholarship states it, not silently passed off as genuine.

The text here is Greek only, verbatim. Nothing is translated, modernised, normalised or silently corrected beyond the documented resolution of the source's own apparatus markup (see "How it was imported" below). Where the source is irregular or a genuine judgement call was made, it is preserved/recorded and flagged in "Known gaps & anomalies" below.

sections.heading: English translation
paragraphs: An English translation of this work is in scope for a separate, concurrently-run import task covering select works of this reader; see this data directory's sibling `-en` work (if present) for its own about.json and provenance. This Greek import does not itself depend on that translation existing.

sections.heading: The edition
paragraphs: Per this XML file's own <sourceDesc>: Aristotelis Opera, Volume 2 (Bekker, ed., Reimer, 1831), Berlin, 1831.

This source has no chapter-level division at all: the entire work is one wrapper div (`subtype="section" n="1249"`, its Bekker starting page) holding exactly 7 bare `

` paragraphs (verified by direct count) - one fewer than the work's traditional 8-chapter division (this transcription runs two of the traditional chapters together into a single paragraph rather than breaking them, most likely at the low-salience break between chs. 6 and 7); each `

` here is imported as its own flat chapter (ch-1..ch-7) rather than forcing an 8th split the source itself does not make. Its Bekker citations are tagged `` (not `unit="page"` as elsewhere in this corpus) - recognised by this importer's value-pattern check (a citation is identified by looking like "1249a", not by its `unit=` attribute literally saying "page").

sections.heading: Digital source
paragraphs: The machine-readable text is the TEI XML file tlg0086.tlg045.perseus-grc2.xml (CTS urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0086.tlg045.perseus-grc2) from the Perseus Digital Library / Open Greek and Latin canonical-greekLit repository. It was fetched once and is bundled with the app (scripts/import-aristotle-rest/raw/tlg0086.tlg045.perseus-grc2.xml); nothing is loaded from the network at runtime.

sections.heading: How it was imported
paragraphs: The importer's generic TEI walker (scripts/import-aristotle-rest-shared/teiWalker.ts) parses this source's own <div type="textpart" subtype="..." n="..."> nesting into a tree, and shapes.ts folds it onto this app's Division scheme: a flat list of Chapters, one per bare source paragraph (this source has no chapter-level division of its own at all).

... (text an editor judged spurious/interpolated, but which the edition still PRINTS, bracketed - the OCT convention) is KEPT verbatim in the reading text, wrapped in square brackets `[...]` (or left unbracketed-but-verbatim on the rare occasion its own printed text already contains a literal bracket, so as not to double them); / keeps the reading and excludes the variant; a bare (no offered) is itself the edition's printed reading and is kept, logged as a crux; ... (an editorial insertion, printed by the edition) is KEPT inline; ... (a modern editorial citation, not Aristotle's own words) is EXCLUDED; / a Bekker-shaped is captured to build Division.ref and removed from the reading prose; any OTHER is discarded entirely (tag and content); a is kept as its literal printed ellipsis text, a contributes no text; ////////<item>/<list>/<cit> (quotations, verse, foreign-language snippets, emphasis, numerals, a quoted work's title, list/table items) are unwrapped - tags stripped, text kept inline as ordinary reading prose, WHETHER nested inside a <p> or printed as a sibling of one (a verse quotation is very often the latter - e.g. this corpus's Empedocles/Homer citations - and is captured as its own implicit paragraph rather than dropped). Every occurrence of all of these except plain milestones/lb/pb is logged in anomalies.json. Entities are decoded and text is NFC-normalised and whitespace-collapsed; the words themselves are otherwise untouched.

In this file: 1 <del> span(s) bracket-kept, 0 <add> insertion(s) kept, 0 bare <sic> crux(es) kept, 0 <choice><sic> variant(s) excluded in favour of <corr>, 0 literal-ellipsis <gap>(s) kept, 0 lacuna <gap>(s) excluded, 0 non-citation <note>(s) discarded.

sections.heading: Reference scheme
paragraphs: Citation is by Chapter and Bekker page/column range: each Chapter's Division.ref is built from the Bekker citation marks found in its own text, in document order (a single value if only one falls inside it, "<first>–<last>" if more than one); this work spans Bekker 1249a–1251b in the standard pagination. 3 chapter(s) carry no Bekker mark of their own in this transcription and have Division.ref = null (flagged individually in anomalies.json, not guessed at).

No printed sub-chapter/line-level reference is attempted for any individual Passage (Passage.ref is null throughout); where a source nests a nameable level below its Chapter (e.g. a "section"), that level's own number survives as Passage.n (e.g. "3", or "3.2" two levels down) rather than being discarded.
